Lower trust issues indicate a decline; signs include increased disease, reduced health and optimism. People are more stressed, less healthy, and less optimistic now compared to before. Trust decreases as people become more willing to save rather than go into debt.

People will save money instead of spending, they are healthier and more optimistic. Immigration is another sign of decline, especially in the Western world, where it reduces social cohesion and lowers the standard of living. Housing prices have risen, making it difficult for young people—especially in China—to afford homes. Fiscal crises also indicate declining standards as governments struggle with public expenditures.

Three theories explain this global decline: financialization, monopoly capitalism, and the shift from consumer to financial capitalism. Financial capitalism focuses on generating money through investments rather than creating wealth by building real goods or services. This leads to a concentration of power in a few monopolies that prioritize speculation over productive work, ultimately undermining economic vitality and social well-being.
